description: Fires when a visitor is on your site for the selected amount of time (e.g. after 30 seconds or 2 minutes). By default the tag fires on all pages; add conditions to fire only on a specific page or under specific criteria. You must specify the duration using the built-in Time on Website variable (value = number of seconds) and set the condition_type once_per_page_view, or once_per_session. See Piwik PRO help: Timer trigger (time on website).

when_to_use: Fire a tag after a visitor has been on the page or site for a set duration
Show messages or surveys after X seconds of engagement
Track time-on-page or delayed conversion signals
common_use_cases: Fire tag after 30 seconds on page
Show exit-intent or offer after 2 minutes
Engagement or survey after 60 seconds on specific pages
best_practices: Set value to the number of seconds (e.g. 30, 60, 120)
Add Page path or Page URL conditions to limit where the timer runs

conditions.description: Array of condition objects. Must include at least one condition using the built-in variable 'Time on Website' (variable_id 4a3cbab8-e239-44ca-b1c9-6c1bc5cc3fbd) with condition_type = once_per_page_view, or once_per_session and value = number of seconds. May include event conditions.

structure.variable_id: For timer duration use 4a3cbab8-e239-44ca-b1c9-6c1bc5cc3fbd (Time on Website); for event conditions use the appropriate variable UUID
structure.condition_type: For the Time on Website condition must be one of: once_per_page_view, once_per_session. For event conditions use the appropriate type (e.g. equals, contains).
structure.value: Number of seconds when using Time on Website variable (e.g. 30, 60, 120)

conditions.recommendation: Include one condition with variable_id 4a3cbab8-e239-44ca-b1c9-6c1bc5cc3fbd (Time on Website), condition_type once_per_page_view | once_per_session, and value = seconds; add Page path or Page URL conditions to limit where the trigger fires.

time_on_website_60_seconds_once_per_page.description: Fire once per page view after 60 seconds

time_on_website_120_seconds_once_per_ses.description: Fire once per session after 2 minutes (120 seconds)

time_on_website_with_page_path.description: Fire after 45 seconds only on blog pages

common_mistakes: Using condition_type other than once_per_page_view, or once_per_session for the Time on Website condition
Setting value in minutes instead of seconds (use seconds, e.g. 120 for 2 minutes)
Omitting the Time on Website condition so the trigger has no duration

possible_causes: condition_type not set to once_per_page_view, or once_per_session for the Time on Website condition
Value not a valid number of seconds
debugging_steps: Ensure one condition uses variable_id 4a3cbab8-e239-44ca-b1c9-6c1bc5cc3fbd with condition_type once_per_page_view, or once_per_session and value = seconds
Use a small value (e.g. 5) to test; ensure the user stays on the page long enough
Test with only the Time on Website condition
